items.statement: IVL will hold 51.8% of MergeCo and become promoter; Blackstone will hold 16.6% and remain promoter

items.statement: Combined entity debt-to-EBITDA will fall to 0.25 from 0.65, providing significant free cash flow for growth and M&A
items.quote: After the merger, our debt-to-EBITDA ratio will fall to 0.25 from 0.65 right now. This gives us significant and strong free cash flow which we will leverage for growth and M&A opportunities.

items.statement: EPL will issue 18.5 crore additional shares; total shares post-merger around 51 crore
items.quote: As part of the transactions, we will issue INR 18.5 crores additional shares and hence the total number of shares would be around INR51 crores.

items.statement: Receivables rose sharply in Q4 FY26 due to imported NPK variants and cooperative invoicing delays; subsidy receivables ~Rs.400 crore, other receivables Rs.300-325 crore, expected to be realized in Q1 FY27.
items.quote: Subsidy because we, that import materials we supplied substantially within this last quar ter. So, subsidy receivable is almost Rs.400 crore and other receivables are in the range of Rs.300 crore to Rs.325 crore

items.statement: Raw material inventory increased from ~Rs.60 crore to ~Rs.93 crore; part of the apparent inventory rise is stock with government cooperatives pending invoicing.
items.quote: Raw material inventory increased from approximately Rs.60 crore to Rs.93 crore. Additionally, the apparent increase is largely due to supplies made to cooperative institutions.

items.statement: Completed IPO in September 2025 raising ₹745 crores used for working capital requirements
items.quote: We complete our IPO in September '25, raising ₹ 745 crores from investors. These funds were used to significantly strengthen our business, notably for our working capital requirements.

items.statement: Cash position INR505 crores at end of Q4 FY26
items.quote: The cash position at the end of the quarter was INR505 crores and a net debt of INR3,531 crores.

items.statement: Net cash flow from operations for FY26 was INR3,601 million and the company was free cash flow positive for the financial year.
items.quote: Net cash flow from operations for the full year stood at a robust INR3,601 million, and we are also free cash flow positive for the financial year.

items.statement: Auditor recommended a one-time impairment of old investments from 2011-2013 for conservative accounting and cleaning of books.
items.quote: those investment which we did the you can say invested long time back in 2011, 2012, 2013 at the analogue era, those investment has become invalid you can say on those way according to the auditors and all and they have recommended to go for impairment for the more of like a cleaning of the books onetime

items.statement: Receivables increased by INR90 crores year-on-year, with INR70-75 crores due to February-March sales not yet due and INR15 crores overdue but collecting in April
items.quote: The increase of about INR90 crores compared to last year's balance sheet if you look at it. From INR90 crores, INR70 crores to INR75 crores is largely because of the sale which has happened in the February and in the March, which has not due even as on 31st March. And about INR15-odd crores is overdue compared to the same bucket of the last year, which is getting the effect in the month of April.

items.statement: Related party exposure is less than INR 100 crores and channel financing for group companies is around 30% of overall business.
items.quote: All related party transactions are reported to the Board and declared in results. Our related party exposure would be, what, lesser than INR 100 crores currently, Sanjay?

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents stood at ₹165.6 billion at period end.
items.quote: Our balance sheet continues to remain very strong with a period-end client funding book at ₹54.5 billion, net worth of ₹61.5 billion, and cash and cash equivalents of ₹165.6 billion, providing ample liquidity and financial flexibility to support growth while navigating regulatory developments.

items.statement: Management is exploring private credit and asset-light models to finance GPU expansion instead of pure equity or debt.
items.quote: Now we are also exploring a variety of private credit asset-light models to bring in rapid expansion to our GPU capabilities.

items.statement: Generated over Rs 10 crore operating cash flow and over Rs 8 crore free cash flow in FY26
items.value: over Rs 10 crore operating, over Rs 8 crore free
items.quote: We were able to generate a cash flow of over Rs. 10 crore from operations and over Rs. 8 crore for as free cash flow for this FY .

items.statement: Operating cash flow generation supported by internal accruals funding Dhule expansion
items.quote: The project will be funded through internal accruals, including accruals over the next six months.

items.statement: No fresh equity issuance planned; Dhule expansion fully funded via internal accruals and term loans
items.quote: The Dhule project is fully funded, with financial closure achieved and term loan disbursements underway.

items.statement: Mahindra acquired 58.96% controlling stake in SML Isuzu from Sumitomo and Isuzu on 1st August 2025.
items.quote: On 1st August 2025, we completed the transaction and acquired 58.96% of controlling stake in SML Isuzu.

items.statement: Operating cash flow generated was INR542 crores in FY26, up 35% year-on-year.
items.quote: During the year, we generated INR542 crores of operating cash, which is up 35% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents stood at INR938 crores at end of March 2026, up 51% from March 2025.
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalents as of the end of March '26 was INR938 crores, up 51% compared to March '25 ending.

items.statement: DSO reduced to 73 days in Q4 FY26, the lowest in the last 12 quarters, after collecting $125 million.
items.quote: During Q4 of '26, we had a very strong collection quarter from our customers, wherein we collected $125 million, which helped us reduce our DSO to 73. This is the lowest DSO we have had in last 12 quarters.

items.statement: Operating cash flow is being conserved and deployed into IPP project development and bank margin requirements.
items.quote: So whatever cash which we are generating from the operations, all cash are mostly conserved and like it is going in the like either development of our own IPP projects or maybe like whenever some margin requirement is there with the banks that we are fulfilling out of it.

items.statement: Full year FY26 recoveries from written-off pool were INR 332 crores, resulting in negative credit cost of 45 bps.
items.quote: For the full year FY'26, total recoveries from return off pool accounts stood at INR 332 crores resulting in a negative credit cost of 45 bps.

items.statement: Q4 FY26 recoveries from written-off pool were INR 167 crores, translating to credit cost of -78 bps.
items.quote: Pleased to report a successful recovery of around INR 167 crores in Q4 FY'26 and around INR330 crores during full year FY26 which translated into a credit cost of - 78 bps in Q4 FY'26 and -45 bps in FY26.

items.statement: FY27 expected recoveries from written-off pool are INR 200-250 crores, with credit cost remaining negative at 15-20 bps.
items.quote: For FY'27 we are expecting around INR 200 crores to INR 250 crores recovery in total.

items.statement: FY27 credit cost expected to remain negative at 15-20 bps due to continued recoveries from written-off pool.
items.quote: So, we still expect the credit cost to remain negative next year in t he range of around 15 to 20 bps

items.statement: Only 2 lakh shares pending conversion; all CCDs matured and converted; no further warrants or dilution expected.
items.quote: Only 2 lakh shares is pending conversion. Only 2 lakh shares which is pending conversion; somebody's request has not come. Otherwise, what you are seeing is a fully diluted shareholding.

items.statement: Q4 cash balances of about INR 1,800 crores are being deployed.
items.quote: Our liquidity is comfortable. Our Q4 cash balances, which we held off about INR 1,800 crores, are being deployed.

items.statement: Working capital cycle improved from 80 days to 55 days in FY26
items.quote: Our working capital cycle improved dramatically from 80 days to 55 days in a single year.

items.statement: Company carrying roughly INR200 crores in treasury
items.quote: Our balance sheet is in good shape. We are carrying roughly INR200 crores in treasury.

items.statement: Debtor days elevated compared to two years ago, focus area for coming year
items.quote: I think our debtor numbers are still elevated in terms of number of days compared to two years ago. So, that is something that that would be a focus area in the coming year.

items.statement: No plan for any preferential issues as of now
items.quote: But, as of now, we have no plan for any kind of preferential issues.

items.statement: Receivables increased by INR 410 crores in FY26; INR 200 crores collected in first 15 days of April due to utility budget delays
items.quote: On the receivable side, I think due to this last minute, say, March numbers, we have missed certain collections. So in the in the first, say, first 15 to 16 days' time, we almost collected around INR 200-odd crores.

items.statement: Receivables rose in March due to pharma clients' fund delays from LC and export payment issues; INR30-40 crore collected in first 10-15 days of April
items.quote: During the month of March specifically, majority of the pharma companies, their funds got stuck because of few LCs or export payment or dollar payment because all these conflicts going on, the rates and all.

items.statement: Normalized receivables cycle is 60-70 days, equivalent to INR60-70 crore
items.quote: Normally it is 60 to 70 days. Looking at this market scenario now, 60 to 70 days is normal in pharma sectors these days now.

items.statement: No equity dilution planned in next 12-18 months
items.quote: Currently we haven't thought of that, sir.

items.statement: CPCL received Gold Shield award from ICAI for excellence in financial reporting
items.quote: And all this has also led CPCL being conferred the Gold Shield award from ICAI for excellence in financial reporting by the institute

items.statement: Generated net cash flow surplus of INR5.5 billion for full year FY26, up 48% year-on-year
items.quote: On the cash flow front, we have generated a strong net cash flow surplus of INR5.5 billion for the full year FY '26, representing a growth of 48% year-on-year.

items.statement: Board declared dividend of Rs 40 per share for FY25-26 subject to shareholder approval at AGM
items.quote: I am also pleased to inform you that at the board meeting today, UTI AMC has declared a dividend of Rs. 40 per share for the Financial Year '25 -26. The same is subject to the approval of shareholders at the ensuing Annual General Meeting.

items.statement: Receivable cycle increased due to US export structure where 50% duty is paid by US entity and customer pays in 30-60 days after receipt
items.quote: That has increased because of US export because the US export that happens, we first supply to our company in USA who imports, pays 50% duty on the product.

items.statement: Thailand average receivable cycle is 30 days, India is 50-60 days, export cycle longer due to shipping time and credit
items.quote: Thailand is overall average 30 days and India is about 50 to 60 days and then some working capital for stocking and finished good and raw material.

items.statement: Working capital borrowing will continue at 7-7.5% to fund profitable business growth
items.quote: Yes, it is good to borrow at 7%, 7.5% and invest in a profitable business, so working capital borrowing will continue.

items.statement: Receivables increased significantly in FY26 due to delayed state fund releases and high revenue growth in the last four months.
items.quote: This led to a pile-up of receivables for the industry in FY26, which significantly increased over the FY opening -- FY25 opening status for receivables.

items.statement: About 80% to 90% of the INR217 crore trade receivables are attributed to the subsidy business.
items.quote: So I would say that about 80% to 90% of it comes from the subsidy business. So it is predominantly coming from our subsidy business.

items.statement: Non-subsidy revenue share grew from 2% in FY20 to 35% in FY26, improving cash flow profile.
items.quote: Our share of the non-subsidy business has increased from 2% in FY20 to 35% in FY26.

items.statement: Company expects cash flows to improve as state payments regularize and revenue mix shifts toward non-subsidy business.
items.quote: As they start regularizing their payments and start paying which we expect imminently. Then we will see good cash flows.

items.statement: Mahindra & Mahindra board representatives Mehta and Balram Yadav joined the board, bringing deep industry experience.
items.quote: Yes, so we are we welcome them and their representation on the board. They come as people with deep industry experience, and they will definitely add value to our discussions and our approach going forward.

items.statement: Board approved buyback of up to 6.4 million shares at INR 1,125 per share for INR 720 crores; promoters and management will not participate
items.value: 6.4 million shares, INR 1,125 per share, INR 720 crores
items.quote: The Board of Directors has approved a proposal to buy back up to 6.4 million equity shares of the company. This 6.4 million equity shares translates to a maximum of 5.76% of the total paid up capital from the shareholders through a tender offer at a price of INR1,125 per equity share for an aggregate consideration not exceeding INR720 crores.

items.statement: DET free cash flow was INR 225 crores in Q4 FY26, representing 163% PAT conversion
items.quote: On the cash front, DET delivered another strong quarter of free cash flow, which came in at INR225 crores, representing a healthy 163% conversion of PAT.

items.statement: Promoters, promoter family, Board members and KMP indicated they will not participate in the buyback
items.quote: I also want to say that the promoters, the members of the promoter family, members of the Board of Directors, key management personnel have all indicated our offer not to participate in this buyback.

items.statement: Prabhakar Atla transitioned from CFO to COO effective April 1; Shrinivas Kulkarni appointed as new CFO
items.quote: Prabhakar Atla, who served his tenure as the Chief Financial Officer, transitioned to be the new Chief Operating Officer as on April 1st with a mandate to strengthen the foundation, transform our core service lines and scale best-in-class delivery models.

name: Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC Ltd

items.statement: New ESOP scheme launched in Q4 FY26 covering about 110 employees at a price close to ₹845.
items.quote: In fact, I must mention we rolled out our ESOP plan this year, well on time at close to about ₹845 price.

items.statement: ESOP impact expected to be ₹8-10 crores per quarter in FY27.
items.quote: However, going forward, there would be an impact of around ₹8 crores to ₹10 crores per quarter in the next year.

items.statement: ESOP charge was INR 93 crore in FY26, dropping to INR 58 crore and INR 28 crore in subsequent years before bottoming out; 90% of ESOPs held by top six management; unallocated pool is 1.7% fully diluted, not expected to be breached in 3-4 ye
items.quote: And hence when we see almost INR 93 crores of that charge came in the first year itself, but then it's dropping down to INR 58 crores and then INR 28 crores and then bottoming out.

items.statement: Board approved a preferential allotment of equity shares worth approximately INR450 crore at the SEBI price of INR483 per share.

items.statement: Operating cash flow impacted by higher working capital due to increased selling and purchase prices in March and ABS inventory addition

So, their volume numbers will go up. lnventory is concerned. Not only the polystyrene inventory is there, but ABS inventory has also come in' 5o, all that adds to that

items.statement: Company maintains debt-free status with net cash position of INR460 crores as on 1st April 2026
items.quote: Company has maintained the status as a debt-free company, and I would like to state that company has still net cash position of cash and cash equivalent of about INR460 crores as on 1st April 2026.

items.statement: Company issued 60,800 equity shares during FY26 under employee stock option program
items.quote: The company issued 60,800 equity shares during the year FY26. Previous year, 124,300 shares issued under the employee stock option program.

items.statement: Trade receivables cycle is about 200 days due to a small family settlement amount from the 2023 takeover; core receivables under six months are minimal and will normalize in FY27.
items.quote: the only reason why our trade receivable cycleis about 200 days, is because there is a very small amount of a family settlement which we hired when we were taking over the company in 2023

items.statement: Payment terms with tier-1 clients are 45 days; some pay in 30 days; quarter-end delays of 10-15 days occur but overall payment cycle under six months is around 45 days.
items.quote: On paper, we have got, we have signed the contract with 45 days of payment with everyone, but there are a few clients who pay in 30 days also. There is a there are a few clients who pay in 45 days also.

items.statement: Unbilled revenue doubled from H1 to H2 due to fleet doubling; 20-22 days needed to submit bills to tier-1 clients due to compliance requirements; unbilled amount will always exist.
items.quote: We have got INR 125 crores worth of machines and closing our taxes in H1, and now ithas gone up to INR 250 odd crores, right? So because of this reason, the unbilled amount has gone up

items.statement: Operating cash flow for FY26 was about 840 crores, similar to 832 crores last year, after accounting for 200-250 crores of Rainforest approval costs.
items.quote: The operating cash flow for the year FY26 is about 840 crores, compared to 832 last year.

items.statement: Net cash balance at group level is about 1,127 crores against gross debt of about 383 crores.
items.quote: So overall, the net cash balance at a group level is about 1,127 crores against gross debt of about 383.

items.statement: Rights issue proceeds at the beginning of the year were used to pay long-term borrowings, increasing equity net worth to about 3,600 crores.
items.quote: This has gone up primarily , obviously, because of the rights issue we had at the beginning of the year, plus the profits that get consolidated in our numbers. With the rights issue proceeds, we paid the long -term borrowings

items.statement: Mitsui Fudosan acquired 49% stake in Blossom project as part of a multi-project strategic partnership with capital infusion already completed.
items.quote: The first part of infusion of capital has happened. This is a multi -project partnership. It started with Blossom, where they have 49% stake, and it's going to be a game-changing partnership from our point of view.

items.statement: Management confirms no advance or provision has been made to Tips Films; costs are expensed in P&L only when songs are released.
items.quote: See follow very clear policy. Once the song is released of any movie album, we would expense it on that day, the entire album cost

items.statement: Transactions with Tips Films are at arm's length and driven by contractual terms.
items.quote: So, I won't be able to share the exact details, but it would be driven by the contractual terms between Tips Films and Tips Music and it would be at arm's length and as per the industry practices.

items.statement: Bank plans fundraise of INR 1,100-1,200 crores within next 2-3 quarters to support growth
items.quote: We should be in the next 2, 3 quarters or next 2 quarters maybe, right, maybe either late Q2 or early Q3, we should be going in for a fundraise because we see that as a bank, we will be continuing to grow at this kind of pace.

items.statement: Cash position healthy at INR1,446 crores as on 31st March 2026
items.quote: Our cash position continues to be healthy at about INR1,446 crores as on 31st March 2026.

items.statement: Sale of buildings Q5 and Q6 will retire all lease rental discounting debt by June 30, 2026, with surplus cash used for AI initiatives
items.quote: The sale of buildings Q5 and Q6 will ensure that we retire all lease rental discounting debt in full by June 30, 2026. The surplus cash will be utilized to accelerate our AI initiatives and to pivot the ecosystem more decisively towards AI.

items.statement: Management thanked investors for support on the rights issue, calling it a significant milestone.
items.quote: I really want to thank each of our investors. You guys have helped us on our rights issue. I think that was a very significant milestone for Mahindra Logistics.

items.quote: We became cash flow positive from a negative 36 crores to a Positive 50 lakhs though, you know, just positive, but that has been a great achievement for the team.

items.statement: Receivables rose to ₹204.34 crore; receivable management is now a strategic priority with sharper collection discipline.
items.quote: However, our focus for the next four quarters remains firmly centred on cash and collection , while our liquidity position remains strong. The receivables have risen to ₹ 204.34 crore.

items.quote: Our total equity expanded to ₹ 419.77 crore while cash and bank balance rose sharply to ₹ 208.57 crore, making this the strongest financial positio n in Fabtech history.

items.statement: Procure ~11% of cleanroom panels from Fabtech Cleanroom Technology (FTCL) and ~15% of air handling units via Advantek, both related parties.
items.quote: We do procure close to 11% of our current procurement of clean room panels from them. Simultaneously, there's also air handling units that FTCL produces, which we also procure from an entity called Advantek and that would be another about 15%.

items.quote: A key milestone this year was our strategic equity infusion of approximately ₹ 230 crores, which fundamentally reset our balance sheet and strengthen our long-term capacity for expansion.

items.statement: Buyback of INR 7.25 crores at INR 100 per share approved, first buyback by company
items.quote: In our recently concluded board meeting, we approved a buyback aggregating to INR 7.25 crores at a price of INR 100 rupees per share.

items.statement: Promoters not participating in buyback, cash conserved for potential acquisitions

items.statement: Receivables increased to INR 25 crores as of March 31, substantial part realized by April 25
items.quote: In fact, these are balances as of 31st of March and today as on 25th of April, I think already a substantial part of that has been realized.

items.statement: Cash parked in mutual funds and public market instruments, MTM losses impacted other income
items.quote: Second half, we see some of this cash has been parked in mutual funds and public market instruments. So, obviously, given the way the market has operated, so there has been an erosion in other income but these are largely MTM losses.

items.quote: Our cash reserves have gone up to 32.5 CR from the open ing position of Rs. 30 CR. i ncreasing the same up by around approximately 2 CR a fter utilization of almost 6 CR towards payout from our internal accruals f or the deals. So, around total of 8 CR of positive cash was generated this year

items.statement: Trade receivables increased from Rs 16 crore to Rs 26-27 crore due to higher Q4 revenue of Rs 37.27 crore
items.quote: If you see, the last quarter's revenues itself have been 37.27 crores, so naturally, the receivables also have gone up during the quarter four.
